title: Dice Semimetric Losses: Optimizing the Dice Score with Soft Labels (MICCAI 2023)
text: Soft Dice and soft IoU are not minimised at prediction = soft target (soft label 0.5: soft Dice is minimised at 1); the semimetric forms DML2 = 1 - 2<x,y>/(2<x,y>+|x-y|_1) and JML2 = 1 - <x,y>/(<x,y>+|x-y|_1) are minimised at x = y and equal the hard-label losses otherwise. Dice % with soft labels (hard / soft Dice / DML1 / DML2): QUBIQ 72.99 / 73.79 / 76.59 / 76.42, LiTS 57.92 / 58.12 / 59.31 / 59.12, KiTS 67.96 / 68.26 / 69.29 / 69.07. Drop-in for soft_iou_loss on fractional area and object coverage (hand check: target 0.5 gives our present loss 0.667 at p=0.5 and 0.5 at p=1, JML2 gives 0 at p=0.5); per-cell weights carry the masks. Blockers: medical organs with rater-averaged labels, not geometric coverage fractions; the repo shows no LICENSE file (re-implement, three lines). Note 2303.16296_dice-semimetric-losses-soft-labels.md (html read).
licence: no LICENSE file seen on the repo page

title: Boundary loss for highly unbalanced segmentation (MIDL 2019)
text: L_B = sum phi_G(q) s(q) with phi_G the signed distance to the GT boundary: a linear function of the prediction that penalises false positives in proportion to their distance, used as (1-a) L_regional + a L_B with a ramped from 0.01 by 0.01 per epoch (alone it collapses to empty). ISLES DSC / HD95 mm: GDL 0.511 / 5.32 -> + boundary 2D 0.644 / 4.80, 3D 0.659 / 2.73; WMH 0.768 / 3.63 -> 0.793 / 2.04 and 0.818 / 1.70; with cross-entropy the gain is mixed; negligible training time. We already store the truncated unsigned distance field of every line layer, so the weight map is free; the graded penalty is a soft tolerance for the 0.5-1 m map offsets; per-cell weights give ignore masks, soft labels only change the 0.5 level set. Blockers: binary medical tasks, no 1-3 pixel structures, needs the regional term and the ramp, negative values clash with Kendall weighting unless kept inside the line group. Note 1812.07032_boundary-loss-distance-weighted-probability.md (ar5iv read).

title: On the Pitfalls of Heteroscedastic Uncertainty Estimation with Probabilistic Neural Networks (ICLR 2022)
text: Gaussian NLL starves cells with large predicted variance (mean gradient (mu-y)/sigma^2); beta-NLL multiplies each term by stopgrad(sigma^(2 beta)): beta=0 is NLL, beta=1 gives the MSE gradient for the mean while sigma is still learned, beta=0.5 recommended, no extra cost. NYUv2 depth RMSE: NLL 0.3854, beta=0.5 0.3789, MSE 0.3776 (LL gets worse, -4.52 to -7.50); dynamics RMSE 0.0192 -> 0.0064 (MSE 0.0068); UCI Yacht 3.56 -> 2.35. Add a log-variance channel to the distance fields and later the velocity head so the planner gets a per-cell scale (registration and occlusion uncertainty); clamp the variance floor. Blockers: no map or segmentation result; the loss value is not a quality measure; a plain Laplace NLL on map vertices (2403.16439) lowered StreamMapNet map AP, so test the mean against Huber first. Note 2203.09168_beta-nll-heteroscedastic-regression.md (html read).
licence: MIT (repo adapts some CC BY-NC and GPL third-party files)

title: Skeleton Recall Loss for Connectivity Conserving and Resource Efficient Segmentation of Thin Tubular Structures (ECCV 2024)
text: One-sided soft recall of the prediction on the 'tubed skeleton' of the GT (skimage thinning plus a diamond-kernel dilation, made on the CPU in the dataloader): L = CE + Dice + w L_SR, w in {0.1, 1}; multi-class capable. nnU-Net Dice / beta0 error: Roads 78.99 / 5.77 (clDice 79.15 / 6.54, SR 79.25 / 4.85), DRIVE 80.87 / 57.0 -> SR 80.99 / 38.75, ToothFairy 71.80 -> 74.42 Dice; TopCoW 13 classes 85.36 -> 86.59 while clDice runs out of memory. Cost: clDice +88 % time and +52 % VRAM, SR +8 % and +2 %. Store the skeleton next to the 0.5 m layers, term = 1 - sum(w tube p)/sum(w tube) with our cell weights. Blockers: for 1-3 cell dividers the skeleton is the mask itself (little new), one HRNet DRIVE run lost 4 Dice points, gains are tenths of a point, no soft-label or ignore-mask handling. Note 2404.03010_skeleton-recall-loss.md (html read).

title: clDice: A Novel Topology-Preserving Loss Function for Tubular Structure Segmentation (CVPR 2021)
text: clDice = harmonic mean of skeleton precision (predicted skeleton inside GT) and skeleton sensitivity (GT skeleton inside prediction); differentiable by a soft skeleton from k rounds of min/max pooling (k >= the largest tube radius, 5-25 in the paper); loss (1-a)(1-soft Dice) + a(1-soft clDice), a in [0, 0.5]. Roads U-Net Dice / clDice 76.23 / 86.83 -> 76.45 / 88.17, Roads FCN 64.84 / 70.79 -> 67.18 / 76.92, DRIVE U-Net 74.25 / 75.71 -> 75.21 / 76.86; < 10 % extra time in the paper, +88 % measured by the Skeleton Recall paper. Comparator for any connectivity term; for 1-3 cell lines the soft skeleton is nearly the identity. Blockers: binary 2D/3D only, per-dataset a and k, Dice sometimes drops, no soft labels or ignore masks. Note 2003.07311_cldice-soft-skeleton-loss.md (ar5iv read).

title: Average Calibration Error: A Differentiable Loss for Improved Reliability in Image Segmentation (MICCAI 2024)
text: Auxiliary loss mL1-ACE: per image and class, 20 probability bins, mean |observed foreground fraction - mean predicted probability| over bins and classes; hard bins are directly differentiable, soft bins use a triangular kernel; Dice + CE + ACE at 1:1:1. Macro-ACE baseline -> hard / soft bins: ACDC 0.131 -> 0.102 / 0.078, BraTS 0.146 -> 0.132 / 0.102, KiTS 0.171 -> 0.131 / 0.109, with Dice unchanged for hard bins (BraTS 0.905 -> 0.905) and up to -1.7 points for soft bins. For calibrated planner-facing cell probabilities: weighted bins with our masks, observed fraction = weighted mean of the soft target. Blockers: medical 3D, no soft labels, ignore masks or thin classes, binning ignores space (nearly empty bins for 1-3 cell lines), no LICENSE file on the repo page. Note 2403.06759_ml1-ace-average-calibration-loss.md (html read).
licence: no LICENSE file seen on the repo page

title: TopoHR: Hierarchical Centerline Representation for Cyclic Topology Reasoning in Driving Scenes with Point-to-Instance Relations (2026)
text: Dense BEV auxiliary supervised with the distance to the nearest centreline clipped at half the lane width, normalised and quantised into 6 bins (discrete distance transform), cross-entropy + Dice. OpenLane-V2 subset_A (DETl / TOPll): no segmentation head 26.8 / 23.1, binary mask 32.6 / 29.8, continuous distance transform 32.0 / 29.8, 6-bin DDT 34.6 / 30.6; 12.6 FPS on an RTX 4090. An arm against our Huber distance regression: K bins of the stored distance field with CE (smeared bin targets for registration tolerance) and an expectation decode for sub-cell position. Blockers: one preprint, one ablation, no variance, the continuous arm is not named as tuned, gain sits on a query-based centreline detector; code 'will be shared'. Note 2604.24119_topohr-discrete-distance-transform-bins.md (html read).

title: Producing and Leveraging Online Map Uncertainty in Trajectory Prediction (CVPR 2024)
text: Laplace NLL on every map vertex of MapTR-family heads, L = sum [log(2b) + |v - mu|/b], regression weight cut to 0.03 (2 for StreamMapNet), gradient clipping at 3. Map AP without -> with: MapTR 0.4488 -> 0.4525, MapTRv2 0.5540 -> 0.5592, Centerline 0.4789 -> 0.4655, StreamMapNet 0.7789 -> 0.7043 (the paper's own labels disagree with two raw rows); trajectory miss rate 8-15 % lower in four of five pairings, up to 50 % faster downstream convergence. Evidence that a heteroscedastic loss can hurt the mean map accuracy, the reason to take beta-NLL not plain NLL. Blockers: vector heads not dense rasters. Note 2403.16439_online-map-uncertainty-laplace-nll-vertices.md (html read).

title: MapTRv2: An End-to-End Framework for Online Vectorized HD Map Construction (title from memory)
text: One-to-one loss 2 L_focal + 5 L_p2p (Manhattan between matched points) + 0.005 L_dir (negative cosine of edge vectors), plus a one-to-many set (K=6) and dense auxiliaries (3 depth CE, 1 BEV-segmentation CE on the rasterised GT map, 2 perspective-view CE). nuScenes mAP: dense supervision none 56.6 -> all 61.5; one-to-many K=0 57.6 -> K=6 61.5; MapTR edge-direction weight 0 / 0.003 / 0.005 / 0.01 = 48.2 / 49.1 / 50.3 / 48.3; permutation-equivalent order 50.3 vs fixed 44.4; MapTRv2-R18 33.7 FPS (RTX 3090). Transfers: the cosine direction term and the evidence that a dense raster CE helps; matching-based losses are excluded by our differentiable rule. Blockers: no ablation of focal or p2p terms, roadmap table inconsistent with the dense ablation. Note 2308.05736_maptrv2-line-losses-dense-bev-aux.md (html read).

title: MapTR: Structured Modeling and Learning for Online Vectorized HD Map Construction (ICLR 2023; title from memory)
text: Source of the permutation-equivalent point-set loss (focal class 2, Manhattan point-to-point 5, edge-direction cosine 0.005) with Hungarian matching; ablations are listed in the MapTRv2 note: fixed order 44.4 vs permutation-equivalent 50.3 mAP, direction weight optimum at 0.005 (48.2 at 0), point2point matching better than Chamfer; MapTR-nano 25.1 FPS, tiny 11.2 FPS on an RTX 3090. See note 2308.05736_maptrv2-line-losses-dense-bev-aux.md (html read).

title: Topograph: An Efficient Graph-Based Framework for Strictly Topology Preserving Image Segmentation (ICLR 2025)
text: Component graph of prediction and GT (TP/TN/FP/FN regions), loss = mean score over critical nodes, proven to imply homotopy equivalence; 2D only, binarised prediction, multi-class by repetition. Test Roads Dice / clDice / BM: 0.817 / 0.711 / 5.64 vs Betti matching 0.818 / 0.707 / 5.91; Buildings 0.769 / 0.590 vs Dice-only 0.777 / 0.611; Cremi tied with clDice. Loss time per call: Topograph 95.9 ms, clDice 9.9, Mosin 233, Betti matching 328, HuTopo 603. Evaluation idea (critical-component counts) is the usable part. Blockers: CPU, linear in batch, no soft labels or masks, gains inside the paper's significance bands. Note 2411.03228_topograph-betti-matching-topology-losses.md (html read).

title: Topologically faithful image segmentation via induced matching of persistence barcodes (Betti matching; ICML 2023)
text: Loss and metric from induced matchings between persistence barcodes of prediction and GT filtrations, combined with Dice (alpha 0.01-0.1); abstract claims better topology on six datasets while keeping volumetric scores (no numbers on the page). In the 3D follow-up (2407.04683) the Betti-matching error falls (VesSAP 3551 -> 2243) while clDice also falls (0.783 -> 0.723): topology bought with overlap. Blockers: CPU persistent homology (328 ms per call in the Topograph comparison), 2D repo and a separate 3D repo, no soft labels. Covered in note 2411.03228_topograph-betti-matching-topology-losses.md (abstract read; tables from other papers).

title: Efficient Betti Matching Enables Topology-Aware 3D Segmentation via Persistent Homology (2024)
text: C++ implementation on Cubical Ripser (implicit matrix reduction, union-find, emergent pairs, parallel barcodes) of the Betti matching loss l_BM = sum 2||q - mu(q)||^2 and DiceBetti l = alpha l_BM + l_Dice; more than 3x faster in the most drastic case, still CPU-bound and cannot be trivially parallelised; gradient assumes no duplicate input values. 3D only (cubical complexes). Context for the cost of persistent-homology losses. Covered in note 2411.03228_topograph-betti-matching-topology-losses.md (html read, first 100k characters).

title: CAPE: Connectivity-Aware Path Enforcement Loss for Curvilinear Structure Delineation (2025)
text: The network predicts a distance map; L = MSE + alpha L_CAPE where, per connected GT vertex pair, Dijkstra finds the GT path, endpoints snap to local minima of the prediction in a 7x7 window, and a second Dijkstra on the prediction inside a path mask dilated by 10 px gives a cost sum y_hat^2 that is the loss. Dice / APLS / TLTS: DRIVE MSE 77.1 / 68.2 / 66.9, clDice 76.2 / 74.5 / 70.5, CAPE 80.3 / 80.2 / 76.4; CREMI MSE 85.4 / 81.9 / 79.5, CAPE 88.7 / 93.6 / 93.5. A gap-probe for distance-field regression. Blockers: discrete path search on the prediction, no cost reported, three small datasets, single runs, no Skeleton Recall baseline, no soft labels or masks. Note 2504.00753_cape-path-loss-on-distance-map.md (html read).

title: ContextLoss: Context Information for Topology-Preserving Segmentation (2025)
text: Pretrain with Dice + CE, then fine-tune about 5 % of the epochs with L = (1-g) L_pixel + g (L_pixel x M) where M is a mask of the pixels around missed and false-positive connections (skeleton of label and prediction split at topological errors, distance transforms), g = 0.2; new metrics e0-Gt and AGS. Roads e0-Gt 0.710 (clDice) -> 0.494, AGS 87.07 -> 89.48, Dice 79.50 -> 79.12; HRF 2.475 -> 1.378; on the 3D CLD set clDice beat the standard variant on gap metrics. Training time Roads 29 min (Dice+CE), 59 (clDice), 71 (ContextLoss). Blockers: needs a pretrained model and a post-processing step, CPU masks, Skeleton Recall not benchmarked, code on GitLab with no licence on the page. (html read, not written up as a note).

title: Aerial Road Segmentation in the Presence of Topological Label Noise (Henry et al.; ICPR 2020)
text: Noise-aware losses for road segmentation from OpenStreetMap-type labels that tolerate omitted labels and misregistration, including a new Bootstrapped Dice loss; the abstract reports consistent gains on two road benchmarks and transfer to crack and cell-membrane delineation. The closest published match to our registration-offset problem for thin lines (the 2020 date is before the requested window). Blockers: abstract page only (no numbers read, no code listed); full text not fetched. (abstract read, not written up as a note).

title: Calibrating Segmentation Networks with Margin-based Label Smoothing (Med. Image Anal. 2023)
text: Replaces the equality constraint of label smoothing / focal / ECP on logit distances by an inequality with margin m: L = CE + 0.1 sum_k max(0, max_j l_j - l_k - m); only m is tuned (5, 8, 10). Mean DSC / ECE: ACDC CE 0.841 / 0.079, CE+Dice 0.827 / 0.137, SVLS 0.701 / 0.176, proposed 0.875 / 0.061; PROMISE ECE 0.411 (CE) -> 0.232; not best on every column (focal wins ECE on MRBrainS and FLARE). Note that CE+Dice degrades calibration, supporting a calibration check of our BCE + Dice mix. Blockers: multi-class logits (softmax), no cost reported, L2 variant worse, code licence not stated. (html read, not written up as a note).

title: Signed Distance Calibration loss (SDC) for segmentation (2025; title from the search result)
text: L = CE + 0.1 L_conf (l1 / l2 between probabilities and a locally smoothed target) + 0.1 L_SDF (predicted vs GT signed distance function). U-Net ACDC DSC / HD95 / ECE: SDC 0.869 / 1.82 / 0.039 vs NACL 0.854 / 2.93 / 0.068; FLARE 0.858 / 4.13 / 0.028; nnU-Net ACDC 0.880 / 1.31 / 0.037. Links calibration to boundary geometry; an SDF head next to the distance field is the same idea as our truncated field. Blockers: formulas of L_conf and L_SDF and the cost are not given on the page, text says lowest ECE but a table row (FCL 0.032) beats it, PROSTATE only 32 volumes, code licence not stated. (html read, not written up as a note).

title: Unified Focal loss: Generalising Dice and cross entropy-based losses to handle class imbalanced medical image segmentation
text: Asymmetric Focal + asymmetric Focal Tversky mix, lambda 0.5, delta 0.6, gamma about 0.5. DRIVE (thin vessels) DSC / IoU: CE 0.789 / 0.652, Dice 0.799 / 0.666, Focal Tversky 0.798 / 0.664, Unified Focal asym 0.803 / 0.671; CVC-ClinicDB Dice 0.867 -> 0.909; BUS2017 Dice 0.767 -> 0.824. The gain on the thin-structure set is within confidence intervals. Blockers: original U-Net only, boundary losses excluded, no soft-label correctness, no ignore masks. Note 2102.04525_unified-focal-loss-focal-tversky.md (html read).

title: A Novel Focal Tversky loss function with improved Attention U-Net for lesion segmentation (ISBI 2019)
text: Tversky index TI = TP/(TP + alpha FN + beta FP) raised to a focal exponent, FTL = sum_c (1 - TI_c)^(1/gamma) with alpha 0.7, beta 0.3, gamma 4/3 (all three from memory; the abstract has no formula). Claims +25.7 % on BUS 2017 (lesions 4.84 % of the image) and +3.6 % on ISIC 2018 over a plain U-Net (relative or absolute not stated). The standard recall-weighted Dice for small structures; no code link on the page. Covered in note 2102.04525_unified-focal-loss-focal-tversky.md (abstract read).

title: The Lovasz-Softmax loss: A tractable surrogate for the optimization of the intersection-over-union measure in neural networks (CVPR 2018)
text: Lovasz extension of the per-class Jaccard loss on the sorted pixel-error vector, class-averaged over classes present in the batch; sort O(p log p). Pascal VOC test mIoU (DeepLab-v2): CE 76.44, CE + equibatch 78.05, Lovasz-Softmax 79.00; binary VOC 77.14 (CE) vs 80.5 (Lovasz hinge); Cityscapes ENet class IoU 58.29 -> 63.06 after fine-tuning from a CE model. Used with CE in occupancy models (see 2405.17429). Blockers: hard labels only, fine-tune stage, no ignore-label discussion in the paper (the common code drops index 255 before the sort), weights between 0 and 1 not supported. Note 1705.08790_lovasz-softmax.md (html read).

title: HDMapNet: An Online HD Map Construction and Evaluation Framework (ICRA 2022, venue from memory)
text: Dense raster design closest to ours: BEV semantic segmentation (cross-entropy in the paper; the repo trains BCEWithLogits with pos_weight 2.13), an instance-embedding head with the discriminative loss (delta_v 0.5, delta_d 3.0, 16 dims) and a direction head (BCE, masked to lane pixels, weight 0.2 in the repo) with vectorisation by DBSCAN and greedy direction tracing. No ablation of individual loss terms in the paper; BEV resolution not stated on the page read. Useful as the class-imbalance baseline (pos_weight) and for the masked direction term. Blockers: no loss ablation, repo is GPL-3.0. (html and repo files read, not written up as a note).

title: StreamMapNet: Streaming Mapping Network for Vectorized Online HD Map Construction (WACV 2024, title and venue from memory)
text: Loss = lambda1 SmoothL1 polyline regression + lambda2 focal classification + lambda3 SmoothL1 transformation loss on propagated queries (lambda1 = 50, lambda2 = 5, lambda3 not given on the page). Av2 new-split mAP (50 m): transformation loss 42.8 -> 43.7; direct prediction 41.7 vs relative 33.7; 14.2 FPS on Av2, 13.2 FPS on nuScenes. Introduces geographically disjoint splits: nuScenes new split overlap 11 % vs 85 % for the original, which shows how much train/val map overlap inflates results (relevant to how we split). Blockers: vector head, no dense loss. (html read, not written up as a note).

title: Stream Query Denoising for Vectorized HD Map Construction (SQD-MapNet; ECCV 2024)
text: Training-only denoising of StreamMapNet queries built from noised previous-frame GT (box shift and scale, decay by matched Chamfer distance); L = L_map + L_denoise with focal and line terms; nuScenes 60x30 m mAP: single frame 59.9, + temporal stream 59.2, + dynamic query noising 62.9, + adaptive temporal matching 63.9; no inference cost; code 'coming soon'. A training-only regulariser for streaming queries, nothing for dense rasters. (html read, not written up as a note).

title: InstaGraM: Instance-level Graph Modeling for Vectorized HD Map Learning (2023)
text: An edge-map decoder predicts a per-class distance-transform map (GT from OpenCV, clipped to 0-10, ReLU + threshold output) with squared L2 loss, weight 1.0, as an auxiliary and as input to graph embeddings. nuScenes mAP ablation: no DT 7.0, DT without positional embedding 20.9, full 41.9 (AP divider 48.3, crossing 33.9, boundary 43.5); no segmentation-aux ablation. Evidence that a distance-transform raster is a usable dense intermediate; the L2 loss without a robust form is the weaker choice against our Huber. (html read, not written up as a note).

title: BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation (MIT; title from memory)
text: Map segmentation head trained with the standard focal loss, one binary segmentation per class (classes can overlap), IoU taken at the best threshold. nuScenes val IoU per class (camera-only / fusion): drivable 81.7 / 85.5, ped crossing 54.8 / 60.5, walkway 58.4 / 67.6, stop line 47.4 / 52.0, carpark 50.7 / 57.0, divider 46.4 / 53.7, mean 56.6 / 62.7. The reference numbers for map layers at 100 m; the loss itself is plain focal BCE with no thin-structure handling. Blockers: BEV resolution of the head not stated on the page, no loss ablation. (html read, not written up as a note).

title: P-MapNet: Far-seeing Map Generator Enhanced by both SDMap and HDMap Priors (title from memory)
text: BEV raster at 0.15 m (60x30 m) and 0.3 m (120x60 m, 240x60 m); the loss of the main segmentation head is not stated on the page read; the HD-map prior is a masked autoencoder pre-trained with pixel-wise CE. Ablation (120x60 m, C+L, IoU): pre-training none 64.1 / 51.4 / 67.4 (divider / crossing / boundary, mIoU 60.97) vs random-mask 65.3 / 52.0 / 68.0 (61.77). Context for the 0.15-0.3 m raster resolution of thin classes. (html read, not written up as a note).
